Representation theory · Lean 4

The third Brauer–Thrall conjecture

Every representation-infinite finite-dimensional algebra over an algebraically closed field has an indecomposable module of each infinite dimension, checked in Lean.

Let k be an algebraically closed field and A a finite-dimensional k-algebra. A is representation-infinite if it has infinitely many isomorphism classes of finite-dimensional indecomposable modules. Let 𝒟 be the category of Kronecker modules, of arbitrary dimension, without a direct summand isomorphic to the simple injective.

Theorem A. If A is representation-infinite, there is a representation embedding F : 𝒟 → Mod A that sends finite-dimensional modules to finite-dimensional modules, commutes with arbitrary direct sums and filtered colimits, and satisfies dim F(T) = dim T for infinite-dimensional T.
Corollary 1.1. For every infinite cardinal κ, A has 2κ pairwise non-isomorphic indecomposable modules of dimension κ with End(M)/rad End(M) ≅ k and (rad End(M))n = 0, for one n ≤ max(30, 4 dim A) independent of κ. For κ ≥ |k| this is the largest possible number.

Verification and provenance

The conjecture

Simson's conjecture, also called the third Brauer–Thrall conjecture, says that a representation-infinite algebra has indecomposable modules of arbitrarily large cardinality. The paper Representation embeddings and the third Brauer–Thrall conjecture settles it over algebraically closed fields. It extends a representation embedding of Bongartz from finite-dimensional Kronecker modules to Kronecker modules of arbitrary dimension, and applies the result to the indecomposable Kronecker modules of Göbel and Simson.

This repository proves the results above and also the cited inputs they use: Bongartz's Theorem 6 and Göbel and Simson's rigid families over infinite fields. The correspondence record maps each numbered statement of the paper to its Lean declarations.
